sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Leapfrog is a real, established electrical, instrumentation, automation and modular-substation EPCC contractor with access to Middle East and Indian industrial projects. Its integrated engineering capability, FY2026 operating revenue of ₹152.34 crore and substantial order backlog make a plausible operating-growth case. They do not yet make an evidence-backed compounder or an actionable value case. Three consecutive negative-CFO years, ₹45.75 crore of receivables more than a year old, a material same-period debt-service representation conflict and uncertain post-IPO available funding dominate the assessment. [E02,E05,E06,E09,E14]

At the stale secondary observed ₹21.50 close of 16 October 2026, the market capitalization is ₹304.85 crore. The apparent 15.57 x reported P/E rises to 26.06 x when all other income is excluded and current shares are used. This is a normalization sensitivity, not a claim that every foreign-exchange gain is artificial. Business Quality is 4.44/10 and Growth Quality 5.00/10; Investment Attractiveness is NS. Quality points are diagnostic, not ranking-eligible while the financial-reliability hold remains. This is a mixed-quality, working-capital-intensive special-situation research candidate, not a supported purchase or compounder designation. [E04,E19]

The decisive variable is collectability and timing of the existing receivable book, not the headline size of the next order. A documented resolution of the FY25 lender/auditor contradiction, substantial aged collections, an updated bridge of unrestricted cash, IPO uses and debt obligations, and a validated trading history could change the classification. A price decline alone would not resolve those gaps. Neither the model’s cash deficits nor a disputed vendor case is presented as proof of current default or wrongdoing. [E08–E12,E17,E20]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Exact issuer: Leapfrog Engineering Services Limited, BSE SME 544797, symbol LESL, ISIN INE0X6O01027. It began as Leapfrog Informatics Private Limited on 9 May 2005, was renamed in 2009 and converted to a public company in June 2024. The latest listed-entity CIN is L74210KA2005PLC036274; the prospectus retains its pre-listing U74210KA2005PLC036274 form. There are no subsidiaries disclosed; related common-control businesses are not consolidated subsidiaries. The research uses standalone Indian GAAP Accounting Standards, not an assumed Ind AS framework. [S1,S2]

Cutoff: 20 October 2026, India-market information available by that date. Retrieval occurred 21 October; the post-cutoff 21 October share-price row was excluded. The selected ₹21.50 is the last independently cross-checked secondary observation, dated 16 October, not a verified 19 October close or live quote. 141,792,000 issued shares and the 6000-share lot are supported by September shareholding and the exact-ISIN 19 October interoperable master. The master’s LESL$ alias and encoded dates/status fields do not turn this BSE security into an NSE listing. [E01,E19]

The analytical horizon runs 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031. The 15% nominal annual equity hurdle is before investor taxes; 12% and 18% are sensitivities. DCF WACC 14–18% is separately specified, not automatically equated to the equity hurdle. The ₹5 lakh liquidity test is illustrative, not a recommended allocation. No orders are contemplated.

G1 is Conditional: stewardship concerns without substantiated severe abuse. G2 is Hold—unresolved: same-year ICRA/CARO debt-service conflict and material balance-confirmation/collection uncertainty. G3 is Hold—unresolved: an IPO exists, but current unrestricted resources and obligation closure are not established. G4 is Hold—unresolved: lot identity is verified but full authoritative trading history and restrictions are not. The detailed gate register states the evidence needed to resolve each issue.

Confidence is High in retrieval of reported P&L, exact share count and auditor wording, Medium in comparable operating growth, normalized profitability and incremental capital proxies, and Low in current financial reliability, funded entry valuation and execution capacity. High confidence that a disclosure was read is not high confidence that an unconfirmed balance will be collected. Overall confidence for an investment conclusion is Low, the weakest material area, not an average.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The 13 factors are assigned once and reused exactly. GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 6, DUR 6, CAP 4, CASH 2, BAL 3, EXEC 5 and EARN 4 describe observed economics and conduct. R, P and L remain NS; they are not replaced by neutral 5 s. D 3 is supported by the material recapitalization/permanent-loss path even though precise investable returns are unverified. Every factor below has at least two material facts, a contrary fact, confidence and evidence references.

BQS =0.20×4+0.20×5+0.12×6+0.10×6+0.12×4+0.10×2+0.08×3+0.08×5 =4.44, displayed 4.4. GQS =0.40×6+0.20×6+0.15×4+0.15×4+0.10×2 =5.00, displayed 5.0. The persistent poor-cash-realization override caps GQS at 5; it does not change this raw 5.00. No governance override is applied because neither GOV≤3 nor an evidenced G1 failure is established. A funding Hold is not mislabeled a funding Fail to manufacture a numeric cap.

IAS uses the exact unrounded BQS 4.44. Its known contribution is 0.25×4.44+0.20×3=1.71; evidence coverage is 45%. Missing weight 55% gives the purely mathematical bound[2.26,7.21]. This is not a statistical interval or a midpoint estimate. IAS stays NS regardless of the upper bound. All ranking flags are false because G2 is a material reliability hold and IAS is incomplete.

REV uses the preselected three-year comparable organic window because a five-year comparable window is unavailable: 13.5036% gives schedule score 6 with zero trajectory adjustment. The most uncertain quality judgments are GOV and CAP. Moving each by one point changes BQS by at most 0.32 jointly; CAP±1 changes raw GQS±0.15, with upside constrained by its cap. This narrow sensitivity cannot resolve the gates or support a ranking distinction. No factor exceeds the Medium-confidence/history ceiling 8.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company designs, procures, integrates, installs and commissions electrical, instrumentation, process automation, fire-protection and related systems. Modular E-house/substation work combines purchased equipment with engineering, assembly, testing and site integration. Revenue comes from negotiated/tendered project scope and delivery milestones, not from a recurring software subscription. The main cost risks are purchased materials, subcontract/site execution, engineering payroll, freight, foreign exchange and rework or warranty obligations. [S1,S2]

FY26 reported mix is contracts ₹143.7061 crore, services ₹5.0390 crore and products ₹3.5926 crore. FY25 was contracts ₹70.9314 crore, services ₹60.1572 crore and products ₹3.5738 crore. The dramatic category shift should not be mistaken for an acquisition or a newly proven high-margin product franchise. Total operating revenue grew 13.12%, while core operating margin fell from 16.59% to 14.81%. Contract-level billings, gross margins and cash margins are not disclosed consistently enough to invent a per-module unit contribution. [E24]

Under the disclosed AS 7 policy, contract revenue is recognized by stage of actual work executed and billable, applying cumulative estimates of contract revenue and costs. Variations, claims and incentives enter only if probable and reliably measurable. Expected overall contract losses are expensed when probable. Goods follow transfer-of-risk recognition and services proportionate/completed performance as appropriate. These judgments create a genuine need for customer confirmation and cash validation; unbilled contract revenue of ₹1.7501 crore and retention ₹7.1879 crore are separate from trade receivables. [S2,Notes 2,15,18]

FY26 geographic export revenue was ₹110.8118 crore,72.74% of operating sales; domestic revenue ₹41.5259 crore. The separately disclosed FOB export figure has a different basis and is not substituted for geographic segment revenue. FY25 top-three customers contributed 52.01%, while nine-month FY26 concentration rose to 73.99%; full FY26 customer concentration is ND. Historic Kuwait/Bahrain reliance and newer Oman/UAE access create both capability evidence and project/country concentration. Payroll 112 plus contract 60 staff as of 30 April 2026 supports an engineering-led operating model, but a point-in-time employee denominator cannot establish productivity growth. [E13,E22]

Unit economics depend heavily on payment terms. CARE describes historical advances and milestone receipts, with much of cash received by dispatch, versus a Bahrain engagement offering credit up to 90 days. A high accounting margin with long acceptance/collection delays can generate a low return on incremental capital. The research therefore treats net cash tied up per rupee of execution, credit days and retained cash as central operating units rather than square feet or backlog alone. [E15]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Leapfrog’s potential advantage is integrated engineering and execution: fewer interfaces for a customer, pre-bid technical preparation, local procurement/assembly capability and experience with Middle East project requirements. CARE attributes up to 60% pre-bid engineering to management’s approach; this is a process claim, not an independently measured cost moat. Named subsequent orders and prior overseas execution provide more persuasive evidence of customer access than a generic market-size forecast. [S1,S11,S14–S19]

The barriers are useful but contestable. Engineering talent can move, equipment is largely sourced, industrial clients tender projects, and one large account can sharply change both annual mix and working capital. No independently reconciled retention/cohort data, repeat-order margins, win rates, sole-source positions or switching costs demonstrate durable pricing power. A large order can make a small company busier while weakening cash resilience. The FY26 decline in core margin and the ageing of receivables are contrary evidence to a simple premium-engineering narrative. MOAT 5 reflects this balance, not an assumption that all contractors are undifferentiated.

Three relevant comparison lenses are retained without forcing a misleading peer multiple table. Konstelec is a closer electrical/instrumentation execution comparator: FY25 standalone sales ₹193.7068 crore, PAT ₹4.2773 crore and CFO−₹14.3967 crore. Its consolidated PAT is different and is not mixed with standalone cash flow. Artson provides a weaker project-execution/capital-risk comparator: FY26 sales ₹163.5835 crore, PAT−₹10.8837 crore and CFO−₹5.4825 crore. Its sponsor relationships, business mix and Ind AS reporting differ from Leapfrog’s. Engineers India is a much larger consultancy/EPC capability and balance-sheet benchmark, identified in the prospectus peer discussion, not a directly transferable market valuation. Its current comparable numerical multiples were not independently obtained and are not invented. [E21]

These peers show that operating scale alone does not ensure cash realization and that project-company losses are economically possible. They do not prove Leapfrog deserves the lowest or highest peer multiple. A durable advantage would require repeated, cash-collected work at attractive incremental returns through changes in customer, country and credit terms.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Comparable restated/latest-basis operating sales were ₹104.1786 crore in FY 23,₹157.8542 crore in FY 24,₹134.6624 crore in FY 25 and ₹152.3377 crore in FY 26. The annual additions are ₹53.6756 crore,−₹23.1918 crore and ₹17.6753 crore. The three-year CAGR is 13.5036%; the FY24–26 two-year CAGR is−1.7629%. FY26 recovery therefore does not yet exceed the FY24 revenue peak. REV 6 follows the 10–<15% schedule, with no discretionary adjustment for the order book or planned factory. [E02,E03]

The original FY23 audited accounts include FY22 revenue ₹41.5914 crore and PAT ₹0.9241 crore, useful evidence of a longer operating history. The FY22 comparative is not fully restated on the prospectus basis, so it is shown separately rather than spliced into a supposedly uniform five-year model. Even five annual revenue observations would provide four, not five, CAGR intervals. Five- and ten-year comparable CAGRs are ND. Nine-month FY26 revenue ₹101.0128 crore and PAT ₹14.1840 crore are already included within FY 26; without a matching prior interim, a comparable TTM is not constructed and the interim is not annualized. [S1,S6]

No acquisition or subsidiary explains the FY23–26 growth perimeter, so the reported movement is organically generated in that practical sense. It is not a clean unit-volume series: project completion timing, customer acceptance, country mix, billable variation scope and purchased-material pass-through all affect revenue. Price/volume/FX translation components are not sufficiently disclosed to allocate them numerically. Foreign-exchange gains in other income are not reclassified as revenue growth. The contract/service category shift is disclosed separately and is not treated as the entire company changing its economic nature. [E04,E24]

Customer concentration was exceptionally high in FY 23–24, and the FY25 decline came after a very large export-led FY24. The fiscal sequence suggests lumpy conversion of a few contracts rather than a smooth secular compounding rate. The opposing evidence is real: FY26 recovered and multiple subsequent named orders broaden visible work. What is still missing is an auditable backlog execution bridge and evidence that the extra orders produce cash after procurement, acceptance and retention, not simply larger receivables.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The accessible runway is specific: continued industrial electrical/instrumentation work, modular substations for overseas projects, domestic industrial contracts and a larger in-house assembly/engineering campus. March 2026 backlog was ₹384.0309 crore, comprising ₹327.1395 crore export and ₹56.8914 crore domestic work. The annual report later mentions ₹377.55 crore without a full intake/execution/cancellation bridge. Neither figure is an audited revenue forecast. Backlog age, cancellation terms, escalation clauses, payment schedules, customer acceptance and project-level margin ranges remain insufficiently disclosed. [E14]

Subsequent orders are kept as an order register, not blindly added to the closing backlog. July Tasneea is USD 7.213139 million with issuer-indicated equivalent ₹67.4428497 crore; Cotmac ₹4.54772 crore includes GST. August ITC supply plus installation totals ₹8.65 crore excluding GST. Trane is USD 336,738.90 with issuer-indicated ₹3.1754478 crore; the later Tasneea order is USD 1.470759 million with no analyst-invented conversion. Different currencies, tax bases and possible overlap prevent a defensible grand total. [S14–S19]

The prospectus prints a ₹27.1036 crore total project cost, with ₹12.3656 crore land,₹13.9789 crore building and ₹0.8591 crore machinery. Those components actually sum to ₹27.2036 crore,₹0.10 crore more than the printed total and its funding split. The mismatch is preserved and stressed, not silently corrected. The new G+2 structure has about 9100 sqft on each floor: ground-floor assembly, then engineering and corporate offices. Existing 5000 sqft assembly is to be replaced by 9100 sqft, with equipment transferred. This does not establish 82% additional revenue capacity, machine throughput or utilization. Building approval was pending at prospectus stage, commencement was targeted for March 2027, and only ₹0.45 crore of IPO project funds was spent by June 30. No later commissioning evidence was located. [E12,E22]

The base path tests growth 15%,15%,15%,12%,10%,10% through FY 32, linking each year to margins, capex and ONWC. The bull path 25%,25%,22%,20%,18%,15% requires significantly better collections as well as execution; it is not simply backed by the area increase. The bear path−15%,0%,5%,7%,7%,7% links customer disruption to lower margins and higher working capital. In all cases the verified June operating-purpose residual is only ₹1.57 crore; project and fee earmarks cannot fund receivables. Growth itself consumes funding.

Recent incremental NOPAT returns of approximately 2.9% are well below the 14–18% cost-of-capital sensitivity. A static growth≈reinvestment×incremental-return consistency check makes clear why 15% growth cannot be funded by recent internal economics alone. The low-profit FY23 starting point produces a better 17.55% long-endpoint proxy but does not establish persistent returns on the most recent ₹69.94 crore capital increase. GQS 5.00, capped at 5 by poor cash realization, distinguishes a visible order opportunity from high-quality value creation.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter-group ownership was 67.26% at 30 September 2026, with no declared pledge. This supplies economic alignment but also control; it does not independently validate procurement or related-party pricing. FY26 disclosed related purchases total ₹15.3759 crore from Leapfrog Automation and Bigleap, related rents ₹0.7821 crore and supplier advances ₹1.2651 crore. Director remuneration increased from ₹0.6966 crore to ₹0.9393 crore. These are disclosed commercial transactions, not evidence of diversion. Market alternatives and contract economics have not been independently validated. [E16]

The June IPO brought ₹79.5984 crore gross fresh proceeds; the ₹8.9148 crore OFS belonged to selling holders, not the company. Of ₹49.36 crore spent by June 30,₹8.78 crore went to Omega Interactive Technologies for branding. Monitoring reports no deviation. The research does not invent a related-party link or call the payment fraudulent. Its speed, scale and uncertain measurable return nevertheless justify scrutiny of deliverables, commercial rationale and allocation discipline while receivables require funding. [S1,S3]

The credit-information history is recurrent rather than a single label. CRISIL in November 2024 revoked an earlier suspension after receiving information and assigned B/Stable and A 4. Its 5 January 2026 update was an information-availability advisory, not a reaffirmation. On 30 January 2026 the rating became issuer-not-cooperating and was withdrawn following a request and banker NOC. CARE’s December 2025 BB/Stable/A 4 assessment is a separate dated opinion and explicitly described stretched liquidity. ICRA’s August 2024 D rating reflected actual term-service delays, not merely noncooperation. [E09,E10]

The promises-versus-delivery record is mixed: established project execution and new named orders support delivery; expected collection normalization after Bahrain credit terms was not confirmed by March 2026 ageing; the new campus remains a March 2027 target with limited June spending. The October 2026 resignation concerned a business-development general manager, not an auditor, and is not converted into a control-failure allegation. Board/AGM appointments are documented, but normal auditor transition is not itself misconduct. [S11,S20–S22]

The pivotal reliability issue is specific: FY25 CARO dated 18 July 2025 says no default in dues to lenders, whereas ICRA in August 2024 described term-loan servicing delay within that same financial year. No loan-wise reconciliation of amount, days, cure timing and reporting definition was found. FY26 no-default and clean bank-return, edit-log and IFC conclusions are real counterevidence for the later period, but cannot logically erase the earlier same-period conflict. GOV 4 and G2 Hold are proportionate; severe governance Avoid is not supported. [E08,E09]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The full statutory packages, not just the headline opinions, were inspected for FY 23–26. Main opinions and separate IFC opinions are unmodified. FY24/25 and FY 26 audit-trail reporting says the feature operated and was preserved, with no tampering instance noted; FY23’s requirement was not yet applicable. CARO statements concerning current-asset returns to banks agree with books. FY23–25 Other Matter paragraphs nevertheless flag debtor/creditor/loan-and-advance confirmation and consequential adjustments; FY26 Note 54 retains confirmation/reconciliation uncertainty. Clean controls and unresolved external balances can coexist. [E08,E09]

Reported FY26 PAT ₹19.5849 crore rises 20.71%, but other income ₹11.1414 crore includes FX ₹7.4083 crore and balance writebacks ₹2.2854 crore. Core EBIT=PBT+finance cost−other income gives ₹22.5634 crore versus ₹22.3438 crore in FY 25, approximately 1% growth. Retaining full finance cost and 28% normalized tax yields core PAT ₹11.69892 crore. Export incentives ₹0.5194 crore may recur, and income-tax interest ₹1.1434 crore within finance cost may not; these are transparent sensitivities, not silently normalized away. [E04]

FY25 comparability matters. The prospectus shows finance cost ₹1.9343 crore and CFO−₹17.1485 crore; the FY26 comparative shows finance cost ₹3.1804 crore and CFO−₹15.9023 crore. Other expenses move oppositely by ₹1.2461 crore, while CFO differs ₹1.2462 crore. This is consistent with financing-cost classification, and after full-finance cash proxies converge within rounding. The latest comparative is used consistently. FY23 PAT restates from ₹0.3415 crore to ₹0.2830 crore and FY 24 from ₹16.0089 crore to ₹16.3927 crore; the restatement includes depreciation/tax and receivable-related corrections. It is not legitimate to cherry-pick original profits with restated cash. [E23]

Cash conversion remains poor after that reconciliation: FY24–26 CFO totals−₹22.0990 crore against PAT ₹52.2020 crore, or−42.33%; cash capex ₹1.9517 crore makes FCF proxy−₹24.0507 crore. Interest is classified in financing, so this FCF proxy is not equity free cash. FY23 CFO ₹12.6452 crore benefited from ₹42.6593 crore customer advances outstanding, not a stable cash yield. FY26 receivables remain ₹107.0673 crore while more-than-one-year balances jump to ₹45.75 crore with no allowance; retention ₹7.1879 crore and unbilled ₹1.7501 crore are additional. Supplier advances ₹20.1894 crore and inventory ₹9.2134 crore also tie up funds. [E05,E06]

The financing-side invested-capital proxy is equity+debt−cash equivalents−nonoperating loans/investments, retaining restricted margin deposits. It rises ₹69.9357 crore between FY 24 and FY 26. An independent asset bridge includes operating working capital, PPE/intangibles, rent deposits, property advances and required bank deposits. Its residual is fully explained by government/deferred-tax assets, other deposits/employee advances less tax/statutory/employee/contract-loss provisions, not an unexplained plug. FY24–26 incremental NOPAT return is 2.8825% on the funding proxy and 2.9319% on the asset bridge. The stable organic perimeter permits this useful CAP substitute; it is not a project IRR. Full yearly rows and residual identities are retained.

March 2026 debt is ₹31.8681 crore and unrestricted cash equivalents only ₹0.0269 crore. The ₹8.9938 crore cash-and-bank heading includes ₹8.9669 crore other bank balances; another ₹1.8629 crore is noncurrent deposits. These are not netted as freely available cash. Booked income tax ₹8.4170 crore, statutory liabilities ₹0.4368 crore and contract-loss provision ₹0.1288 crore are paid once in all modeled FY27 paths unless an explicitly unverified prepaid-relief sensitivity is selected. Future earnings tax is separate. Employee net liability ₹0.8105 crore is retained as a senior terminal claim; pension assets are not added twice. AS 19 rent stays in operating expense, no invented lease asset/value is added, and operating land is never valued separately from the operating enterprise. [E18]

IPO shares rise from 107.184 million to 141.792 million: 32.2884% share-count expansion and 24.4076% ownership dilution are different measures. Historical bonus/split adjustments are non-economic and are not another cash raise. Current-share reported EPS is ₹1.3812 rather than the historical weighted-average ₹1.83; core normalized current-share EPS is approximately ₹0.8251. No additional warrants, ESOP conversion or NCI is invented. [S1,S2,S7]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The valuation starts with cash feasibility, then an enterprise-to-equity bridge. At ₹21.50 and 141.792 million shares, market cap is ₹304.8528 crore. Reported FY26 P/E15.5657 x and core-normalized 26.0582 x are meaningful cross-checks, but neither establishes value. A March-debt-only EV/EBITDA diagnostic is 14.6268 x; it is not a current post-IPO EV because current available cash, debt and earmark closure are unknown. No peer market premium is presumed. [E04,E19]

June 30 monitoring verifies ₹30.24 crore remaining: project ₹26.55 crore, fees ₹2.12 crore and operating-purpose WC/GCP ₹1.57 crore. Already spent ₹34.66 crore WC and ₹8.78 crore branding are not added again as cash or automatically releasable assets. The potential ₹15 crore bridge is a sanctioned limit, not a fresh source; actual draw and repayment are ND. The entire remaining project envelope is conservatively withheld from operating liquidity. A disclosed ₹3.0413 crore internal-accrual reimbursement could release cash within the issuer rather than cause a new external capex burn; any bridge repayment would reduce a drawn loan. Actual use/draw evidence is missing, so the model grants no speculative release and makes no claim that every earmarked rupee is additional external capex. It does not subtract the ₹15 crore bridge twice. March debt/working-capital balances are conservative proxies for a post-June bridge, not claimed October facts. [E11,E12]

The model runs June 30 to October 20 entry, fiscal year-ends and October 20,2031 terminal, with actual year-day denominators including leap years. No post-terminal cash need governs the investor horizon. Minimum operating cash is max(₹1.5 crore,1% of modeled annual revenue), explicitly retained at terminal. Base margins 14.5%, working-capital ratios 68% tapering to 60%, operating capex 1.8% of sales and 10 x exit EBIT already require collection discipline. Bear margins 9–11%, elevated working-capital ratios 85% tapering to 78%, a 25% project overrun,₹15 crore collection shortfall and separate vendor/portal claims stress linked economics. Bull margins 16–17%, working-capital ratios 60% falling to 50% and 13 x exit EBIT require much stronger execution and cash conversion. Tax 28%, debt amortization and financing costs are explicit. [E20]

Every ordinary case breaches the conservative operating cash floor before entry. A separate hypothetical 50% working-capital-intensity case has no cash-floor breach, a meaningful positive counterweight, but those collections are not observed or verified current funding. This demonstrates that the specified public-evidence bridge cannot substantiate financing, not that the issuer was actually insolvent on October 20. Ordinary IRRs, ordinary entry prices and even conditional non-rescue IRRs therefore remain null. Negative algebraic cash is not described as available debt. A separate rescue issues shares at 35% below the reference price with 5% fees, injects proceeds before the modeled deficit, and reports gross/net proceeds, shares, expansion and holder dilution. These are counterfactual stress diagnostics, not an available financing plan or investment recommendation.

A separate non-rescue FCFF DCF tests 14/16/18% WACC and 3/4/5% terminal growth, with terminal ROIC 18% defined on total operating capital including required cash. Terminal reinvestmentg/ROIC therefore includes cash-reserve growth; the explicit period also retains cash. Signed entry cash minus the reserve preserves the opening deficit. Earmarked project cash is added only against future included project spending; fee earmarks and their matched issue fees are excluded together. Terminal-value share is disclosed for every cell. Rescue DCF is omitted because an unfunded recapitalization cannot be mistaken for an entry valuation.

The 25-cell growth/exit-multiple matrix retains full funding rows, and linked stresses include 30 additional collection days,25% project overrun,25% BG call, claim loss, margin−3 pp and 25% noncollection of aged receivables. A further case pays down ₹30.366 crore of existing working-capital debt if renewal fails, reducing subsequent debt and interest; the date is an analyst stress assumption, not an asserted contractual maturity. Main cases depend on continued renewal, which remains unverified. The ₹0.10 crore project-component discrepancy is separately stressed. 12/15/18% hurdle reverse scans test 0–60% growth, but no verified funded bracket exists; required growth and entry ranges stay null. An endpoint is not reported as a solved market expectation. A robust price conclusion awaits funding and reliability evidence, not a more elaborate spreadsheet.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest credible bear case begins with a large customer delaying certification or payment. Procurement and site spending continue, supplier credit tightens, bank utilization rises and a bond/guarantee call or vendor settlement competes for the same cash. Slower execution reduces fixed-cost absorption; contractual rework and exchange movements can erode the margin precisely when old receivables fail to convert. A recapitalization at a depressed price transfers value away from existing holders even if the company survives. This is a permanent-loss path, distinct from a temporary quoted drawdown. [E06,E09,E15,E17,E20]

The key thesis-break variable is cash collection of already recognized earnings. Receivables older than a year ₹45.75 crore equal a substantial portion of equity. A 25% noncollection stress on that pool consumes ₹11.4375 crore of funding, without also deducting the same amount from modeled EBIT. Guarantees ₹18.3455 crore are contingent, not all payable debt; the separate 25% call stress is ₹4.586375 crore and does not assume release of margin deposits as an offset. Booked taxes are paid in all cases, while portal demands ₹1.2594 crore enter only claim stresses. [E06,E17,E18]

Mega Power requires careful legal distinction. The 2019 tribunal dismissed the claim on maintainability; the counterclaim was also dismissed, while substantive findings calculated entitlement of about ₹8.9972 crore. The 2022 commercial-court judgment dismissed Leapfrog’s challenge and preserved the award, with adverse merits findings against aspects of its nonperformance argument. The offer document/FY26 accounts describe pending High Court appeals 278/2022 and 124/2023 and disputed claim. That combination is neither a clean exoneration on merits nor proof of a currently enforceable ₹8.9972 crore payable award; current appeal/stay/enforcement status was not obtained. The model uses a contingent payment stress, not an adjudicated-current-liability assertion. [J1,S1,S2]

The opposing evidence is meaningful: core EBIT is positive, new orders show market access, IPO equity adds resilience and FY26 audit/control conclusions are clean. If aged receivables are subsequently collected and current obligations are demonstrably funded, the stressed path may be too harsh. Accordingly impairment risk is High, not a claim of certain loss or fraud. D 3 reflects material downside/recapitalization exposure; G3 remains an unresolved Hold rather than an evidenced present funding failure. No probability of litigation loss or rescue availability is invented.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold stock-price outcome over five years requires 37.97% annual growth; tenfold requires 58.49%. These are per-share outcomes, not simply five or ten times today’s order book. At the current share count, a 15 x terminal P/E and 10% common net margin,5 x price would require PAT ₹101.6176 crore and revenue ₹1016.176 crore; 10 x would require PAT ₹203.2352 crore and revenue ₹2032.352 crore. Any dilution raises the required company earnings further. [Model calculation from E01,E19]

Those revenues are approximately 6.67 x and 13.34 x FY26 sales. They would demand major customer diversification, large procurement/working-capital funding, repeatable project margins and more execution capacity than is demonstrated by a replacement assembly facility. The 15 x P/E is a sensitivity, not a justified inevitable market rating. A lower multiple or less than 10% cash-supported margin makes the test more demanding; backlog does not solve the capital requirement.

The base path and even the optimistic growth path have unverified financing and pre-entry cash-floor deficits on the documented bridge. Recent incremental capital returns near 2.9% and negative cumulative cash conversion do not support self-funded scaling of this magnitude. The outcome is therefore Speculative / unsupported on current evidence. It is mathematically possible for future contracts, collections and capital access to change the result, but there is no supported probability or multibagger designation. Dividends are not assumed, and retained cash is not counted again as a dividend.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
The monitoring table below is a research checklist, not an automated reminder or trading instruction. Thresholds are tied to this issuer’s balances and commitments rather than generic rules.

1. FY25 lender/auditor reconciliation: baseline is the August 2024 ICRA delay versus 18 July 2025 CARO no-default. Resolve with loan-wise dates, amounts and reporting definitions. Continued silence leaves G2 on Hold; evidence of intentional material misstatement would require a fresh integrity assessment, not an automatic inference today.
2. Aged collections: baseline ₹45.75 crore over one year and ₹58.71 crore over six months at March 2026. Seek customer-confirmed receipts and balances in the next published financial set. An increase while revenue grows is an alert; material confirmed nonrecoverability without adequate provisioning would break the stated asset-supported thesis.
3. CFO and working capital: baseline three-year CFO−₹22.10 crore and FY 26 core ONWC ₹94.17 crore. A positive half-year alone is not enough; require a sustained collection bridge not funded by unpaid suppliers. Higher aged balances together with additional borrowing is a red flag.
4. IPO residual and bridge: reconcile June 30 ₹30.24 crore by object, including ₹26.55 crore project and ₹2.12 crore fees. Obtain actual ₹15 crore bridge draw/repayment, subsequent bank limits and usable balances. A known overdue obligation or unmet essential cash need would escalate G3, whereas verified fresh resources could clear it.
5. Opening tax/claims: establish payment or lawful settlement of booked income tax ₹8.417 crore and other statutory amounts separately from ₹1.2594 crore portal demands. Track Mega Power appeal/stay/enforcement with a current official order; do not infer outcome from a scheduled hearing date.
6. Campus delivery: baseline ₹0.45 crore IPO project spend at June 30, approvals pending in prospectus, target March 2027. Monitor approval, construction, commissioning and utilization separately. A delay requires revised spending/funding and customer delivery assumptions, not an immediate fabrication allegation.
7. Order conversion: reconcile ₹384.03 crore March backlog and subsequent named orders to execution, cancellation, margin and cash. An intake announcement without terms is not sufficient. Concentration beyond the nine-month top-three 73.99% requires additional counterparty attention.
8. Governance/deployment: verify branding outputs for ₹8.78 crore and commercial RPT terms; monitor rating information cooperation and any new capital raising. Unsupported growth promotion without cash evidence is not a catalyst.
9. Tradability: obtain current BSE restrictions, verified 20/60-session tape, spreads and whole-lot depth. Recalculate the illustrative 3-/4-lot execution test; missing dates remain missing, not zero volume.

Review upon the next results, monitoring report, rating action or material order/legal disclosure. A normal share-price swing does not itself change BQS or GQS; a changed funding/collection fact can.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Hold — unresolved. Research priority is financial reconciliation and collections, not a wait-for-a-cheaper-price recommendation. BQS 4.44 and GQS 5.00 describe mixed-to-weak demonstrated quality; IAS is NS because R, P and L are unscoreable and critical gates remain unresolved. The record is excluded from numerical business, growth and investment rankings while financial reliability is material to the conclusions. The compounder criteria are not met by a wide margin: GOV, MOAT, CAP, CASH and BAL do not meet required levels. [Score audit]

This is not Avoid — governance: no substantiated severe diversion or minority abuse was established. It is not a proven current default: the model uses conservative March proxies and verified June earmarks because later financeability is unverified. The historical ICRA delay is real and cannot be ignored, but historical default and current hypothetical shortfall are different claims. A holder would need verified tax, liquidity and portfolio context before deriving an exit decision; this research does not invent holdings or execute a trade.

A favorable reassessment would require a coherent lender/auditor reconciliation, meaningful aged-customer collection evidence, transparent post-June cash/debt/IPO deployment, bridge settlement and a funded linked stress case. Subsequent clean reporting would strengthen confidence but would not retroactively erase historical differences without explanation. Validated official trading data and current restrictions are also necessary for a new-position implementation score.

If these conditions improve, rerun the same operating/capital assumptions and 15% hurdle with current dated price rather than quietly replacing the historical reference. If margins or collections disappoint, lower terminal economics and higher dilution must be modeled together. Neither headline backlog, promoter ownership nor low reported P/E can compensate for a missing financing bridge.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The source ledger identifies every material original disclosure, date, exact URL, hash where locally retrieved and page/note locator. Original issuer PDFs, OCR, HTML, court text copies and shareholder detail are excluded from analytical backup files; the backups retain safe financial extracts, source URLs/hashes and reproducible calculations. Reproduction validates the arithmetic and assembly from those extracts, not a fresh authentication of original sources. Reported facts, calculations, management statements and analyst assumptions are labeled V/C/M/A in the evidence register.

Primary company evidence includes the final prospectus, original FY23–25 audit packages, FY26 annual report and financial notes, June IPO monitoring, September shareholding and subsequent order/governance filings. Rating rationales were read separately at their actual dates. The court judgment is a legal-document mirror and does not establish the current High Court docket. Secondary price sources are used only with explicit stale/incomplete qualifications; an unavailable official BSE file is not substituted with a fabricated zero-print observation.

Financial units are ₹crore unless identified otherwise. Core EBIT excludes all other income and adds back finance cost to PBT; normalized tax is 28%. Core ONWC excludes cash, debt and tax balances, and includes operating advances, retention and unbilled assets. Restricted deposits remain invested capital. The historical IC residual is explicitly reconciled. CFO−cash capex is a reported FCF proxy before financing-classified interest, not FCFE. Current shares, historical weighted-average EPS and hypothetical rescue dilution remain distinct.

The dominant open questions are precise: loan-wise FY25 debt-service reconciliation; customer-confirmed recovery and provisioning for old receivables; current unrestricted cash/debt and sanctioned usable headroom; actual bridge draw/settlement; post-June IPO spending and project approval/completion; terms and cancellation/collection timing of backlog; current litigation enforceability/stay; and validated official tape/restrictions. Missing project/cohort economics are not filled with promotional capacity percentages. Comparable peer prices and complete latest peer filing coverage are insufficient for a live peer-multiple ranking.

Assumptions are intentionally testable: working-capital intensity, margins, growth, operating capex, interest, project timing, claim payments, exit multiples, WACC, terminal growth and reserve-inclusive terminal ROIC. No future financing is described as committed. No precision in model outputs should be read as precision in forecast truth. This is independent educational research, not personalized financial advice, a guarantee or an instruction to transact.
